1.pericope_label: Who is this that cometh from Edom
debates: Who the conqueror coming from Edom is
Whether the passage was fulfilled in the wars of Judas Maccabaeus
Whether Edom is a literal enemy or a representative one
outliers: Clarke rules out the Maccabean reading on geographical grounds that the other voices do not raise
themes: A separate oracle standing on its own
Names that carry their own imagery
Majesty employed in servile work
Blood that is not the conquerors own

3.pericope_label: Trodden alone, and the year of redemption
debates: Whether the winepress is the wrath Christ bore or the wrath he executes
Whether the verbs are past or future
Whether the year is of the redeemed or of redemption
outliers: Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch put the whole slaughter in the past where the received rendering leaves it future
themes: Alone, without servants or allies
A symbol read in two directions
A date fixed in the heart
Textual traces of an irregular verb

5.pericope_label: No helper, and the cup of fury
debates: Whether the text reads my fury or my righteousness
Whether the passage may be applied to the passion of Christ
Whether the imagery remains that of battle or shifts to the cup
outliers: Ellicott allows the passion reading only as a remote analogy and denies it is the sense of the passage
themes: Deliverance shown to be Gods alone
Help looked for to test men, not from need
A liturgical application examined
Strength brought down to the dust

7.pericope_label: The lovingkindnesses recounted, and a people expected to be true
debates: Whether the section is a psalm, a prayer, or a formulary of humiliation
Who the Saviour of the eighth verse is
What the expectation that they would not lie implies about the covenant
outliers: Wesley identifies the Saviour as Christ against the historical deliverers others might name
themes: Praise before petition
Goodness from God and goodness in God
Mercies of others counted as ones own
A covenant resting on an expectation

9.pericope_label: The angel of his presence, and the Spirit that was vexed
debates: Whether the text reads he was afflicted or there was no affliction
Who the angel of his presence is
Whether the verse distinguishes three persons
outliers: Wesley identifies the angel with Christ where Ellicott leaves him an angel of mediation
themes: Sympathy ascribed to God after the manner of men
Affliction neither by chance nor in wrath
A Spirit who can be grieved
Love compelled to show itself as wrath

11.pericope_label: The days of old remembered, and the sea led through
debates: Whether God or the people are the ones who remember
Whether the shepherd is Moses alone or the leaders together
In whom the holy Spirit was put
outliers: Gill makes God the subject of the remembering where Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch make it Israel
themes: Memory as an act of repentance
Agency placed behind the visible leader
A sea crossed as easily as a plain
Description turning into address

15.pericope_label: Look down from heaven, for thou art our father
debates: Whether the request is for notice or for a special regard
Whether the mention of Abraham is denial of his help or of his knowledge
How far the fatherhood claimed here reaches
outliers: Ellicott finds a remonstrance in the address to heaven where Henry finds an encouragement
themes: Words given to a people for their time of need
Holiness and glory as one habitation
Ancestry set aside for adoption
A Father who is also Redeemer

17.pericope_label: Hardened from thy fear, and sunk to the level of the heathen
debates: Whether God makes men err or permits them to err
Who possessed the sanctuary for a little while
Whether the last verse claims covenant standing or laments its loss
outliers: Ellicott removes the supplied word thine and reverses the plea that Gill and Wesley build on it
themes: Confession that does not shift the blame
Hardening described as judicial withdrawal
A promise of for ever measured against centuries
A people indistinguishable from those who never knew God
